text:
anya: heads up — vendor sent epimetheus-9b v1.2 for onboarding. license text attached, looks custom. quick Q: can we quantize + offer as a hosted model or push quantized weights to Dedicated customers?

sam-legal: can you paste the license link? some custom licenses have non-export or no-derivatives clauses. cc @anya

anya: link: https://example.com/epimetheus-1.0.txt — short version: 'research use only' clause + 'redistribution prohibited without express consent' + attribution required. file attached in the ticket.

licensing-bot: LICENSE SUMMARY — Epimetheus-1.0: research-only; redistribution prohibited; attribution required. Recommend legal review for commercial/hosting. (automated)

julie: rough experimental note: int8 quant gave ~2.5% F1 drop on our STS eval, int4 was worse. That said, int8 reduces cost ~3.3x in our bench. If license blocks distributing weights, we could still offer an API-backed hosted variant with quantized runtime internally.

mike: infra note: Dedicated customers sometimes want the model placed in their VPC or on-prem. If redistribution prohibited, we can't hand them the weights. We could still deploy inside their Dedicated cluster if customer signs an MSA that includes a host-only runtime clause, but need legal ok.

sam-legal: reading the license: 'redistribution prohibited' means we can run the model for customers (service) but cannot distribute weights or derivative files. Important: "research use only" prohibits commercial use — that blocks us from offering it to paying customers at all unless vendor grants a commercial license. We need an explicit commercial sublicense or vendor amendment.

anya: ok — so two paths: 1) ask vendor for commercial license + redistribution carve-outs for quantized derivatives; 2) if vendor refuses, offer internal hosted inference only for evals/experiments, not to customers. Correct?

sam-legal: yes. Additional nuance: some vendors allow 'non-derivative' distribution but permit model access via API (service provider model). Others allow derivative weights (quantized) but require attribution and a share-back. Ask vendor: (a) permit quantized derivatives for commercial service, (b) permit distribution to Dedicated customers under NDA, (c) attribution text and whether share-back of weights required.

julie: will draft a concise email to vendor asking those three bullets, plus a simple ML appendix showing the quantization path we use (int8 per-channel, PTQ, no weight fusion) so they know what 'derivative' means. sample snippet I plan to include:

```
Quantization: per-channel symmetric INT8, PTQ; KV cache preserved, no weight sharing.
Artifacts: quantized checkpoints (.pt) + quant-spec JSON
```

mike: one more infra ask: if vendor allows quantized derivatives but forbids redistribution, can we provide Dedicated customers with a runtime image that contains the quantized weights but marked as not-extractable? Practically hard — customers with access can dump memory. We'll likely need a contractual "host only" requirement and technical measures (HSM + no shell access). Ping infra-security.

sasha: assign to @legal: please escalate, vendor negotiation priority medium-high. we want to avoid delaying eval benchmarks. anya — can you prod vendor for a reply within 72h and paste our benchmark delta numbers?

anya: yep. I'll send vendor email now, attach eval numbers and the quant appendix. copying the draft here for review.

anya: DRAFT -> "Hi Epimetheus team — thanks for sharing v1.2. We're evaluating for production. Before we proceed could you confirm: (1) whether commercial use and hosting by a third-party offering a paid service is permitted; (2) whether quantized derivative weights (INT8/PTQ) can be created and used in commercial service; (3) whether redistribution of quantized checkpoints to Dedicated/on-prem customers is allowed, and if not, whether a host-only exception can be negotiated; (4) any required attribution text and share-back obligations. Thanks — Anya @ Redwood Inference."

sam-legal: good. add a line asking for sample license language if they are open to a commercial addendum. also ask whether they require token-level logging or provenance obligations.

julie: once vendor responds, we should run a small compliance experiment: create a reproducible quant pipeline, record artifacts, and compute perf/quality vs baseline, document everything in the model card. that'll make legal sign-off faster.

mike: noted. infra-security: I'll open a ticket to evaluate "host-only" deployment feasibility (HSM + no-shell + encrypted storage + attestation).

licensing-bot: created ticket ML-LEGAL-4021 and infra ticket INFSEC-919.

anya: thanks everyone — will update thread when vendor responds. :thumbsup:
